goal.text: The project coordinator gets a repair queue each Saturday afternoon, so nobody is promised a bike back before the work can be done.
cites: [A:A01 "so nobody is promised a bike back before the work can be done"]

agent_checkable.metric: Promised dates earlier than the queue's bench time allows
agent_checkable.check: A script adds up bench minutes in queue order and compares each promised date (Q01).
cites: [A:A01 "Q01 a promised date is never earlier than the queue's bench time allows (blocker)."]

agent_checkable.metric: Brake or steering jobs behind another kind of job
agent_checkable.check: A script checks the queue order (Q02).

agent_checkable.metric: Jobs over 90 bench minutes given a single day
agent_checkable.check: A script checks every job over 90 bench minutes is split over two days (Q07).
cites: [A:A01 "No split job is promised for one day."]

agent_checkable.metric: Waiting-for-parts rows with a promised date
agent_checkable.check: A script finds every row marked waiting for parts and checks its date is empty (Q06).
cites: [A:A01 "Every waiting-for-parts bike has no date until its part arrives."]

outcome.metric: Bikes promised back earlier than the work allows
cites: [A:A01 "No bike promised back earlier than the work allows, over a term."]

outcome.metric: Steering jobs done the same Saturday
cites: [A:A01 "Every steering job is done the same Saturday."]

users_and_stakeholders.interest: Work through the queue in order.
cites: [A:A01 "Repair volunteers (users: work through the queue in order)."]

users_and_stakeholders.interest: Signs off the queue each Saturday afternoon.
cites: [A:A01 "Project coordinator (approver: signs off the queue each Saturday afternoon)."]

users_and_stakeholders.interest: Their bike back on the date they were given.
Orders parts on Mondays and needs to know what is waiting.
cites: [A:A01 "Parts volunteer (stakeholder: orders parts on Mondays and needs to know what is waiting)."]

steps: The coordinator sorts the slips by hand.
The coordinator estimates each job from memory.
The coordinator writes the queue on a whiteboard.
Parts are ordered on Mondays from one supplier.
Long wheel builds are started when a volunteer is free.
problems: Estimates from memory are often an hour out.
A bike with a loose headset waited two weekends.
A bike waiting for a part can sit in the shed for a week, and nobody tells the customer until they ask.
Long wheel builds are started late on a Saturday and left half done.
cites: [A:A01 "estimates from memory are often an hour out"]
[A:A01 "Out: buying parts, bike donations, the Tuesday youth session."]

inputs.description: Typed drop-off forms, about 25 each saturday. Each form has a 'needed for work' box and a line for parts the customer brought.
inputs.format: plain text, one form per ticket
constraints: The customer's description of the fault
Parts the customer brought, if any
cites: [S:S01 §whole file]

glossary.meaning: The standard time a job takes, from the bench-time table.
cites: [A:A01 "Bench minutes: the standard time a job takes, from the bench-time table."]

glossary.meaning: The bearings that let the handlebars turn.
The drop-off form a customer fills in.
The box on the form a customer ticks when they ride the bike to work.
cites: [A:A01 "Needed for work: the box on the form a customer ticks when they ride the bike to work."]

glossary.meaning: A job that cannot start until a part arrives.
cites: [A:A01 "Waiting for parts: a job that cannot start until a part arrives."]

glossary.meaning: Lacing a new wheel from a rim, spokes and a hub.
cites: [A:A01 "Wheel build: threading a new wheel from a rim, spokes and a hub."]

glossary.meaning: Adjusting the gears so each click moves one sprocket.
cites: [A:A01 "Indexing: adjusting the gears so each click moves one sprocket."]

glossary.meaning: A job worked over two days because it is longer than 90 bench minutes.
cites: [A:A01 "Split job: a job worked over two days because it is longer than 90 bench minutes."]

acceptance_tests.words: I give it a day with a 120-minute wheel build, and the build is split over two days.
cites: [A:A01 "I give it a day with a 120-minute wheel build, and the build is split over two days."]

acceptance_tests.words: I give it a form whose part is not in stock, and the bike is listed as waiting for parts with no date.
cites: [A:A01 "I give it a form whose part is not in stock, and the bike is listed as waiting for parts with no date."]

acceptance_tests.words: I give it two brake jobs, one needed for work, and the work one comes first.

ranks.what: Reference documents in the context pack
Official documentation on the maker's own site

confidence.high: The row quotes the form and the bench-time table line that decided it.
confidence.medium: A reputable secondary source; not expected here.
confidence.low: Inferred or one weak source; such a row is marked 'ask the workshop' and raised as a question.

conflicts: The higher rank wins within its own area.
A conflict the ranks do not settle is reported with both citations, never decided silently.

output.description: A repair queue, one row per drop-off form, in working order. A slip with no fault description is refused as 'ask the customer'. A job over 90 bench minutes is shown on both of its days; a bike waiting for a part is listed at the end with no promised date.
output.format: Table, one row per ticket, in queue order

fields.name: ticket
fields.description: The ticket number from the form.

fields.name: bike
fields.description: The bike as the form describes it.

fields.name: job_type
fields.description: brakes, steering, gears, wheels, punctures or other.

fields.name: reason
fields.description: One sentence, quoting the customer's description.

fields.name: needed_for_work
fields.description: yes or no, from the form's box.

fields.name: parts
fields.description: 'waiting for parts' with the part named, or empty.

fields.name: split
fields.description: For a job over 90 bench minutes, the two days it is worked on.

cites: [A:A01 "A slip with no fault description is refused as 'ask the customer'."]

rules.statement: A promised date is never earlier than the queue's bench time allows.
cites: [A:A01 "Q01 a promised date is never earlier than the queue's bench time allows (blocker)."]

rules.statement: A brake or steering job goes ahead of every other job.
cites: [A:A01 "Q02 a brake or steering job goes ahead of every other job (major)."]

rules.statement: Every row quotes the customer's description from the form.
cites: [A:A01 "Q03 every row quotes the customer's description from the form (major)."]

rules.statement: Bench minutes come from the bench-time table, never a guess.
cites: [A:A01 "Q04 bench minutes come from the bench-time table, never a guess"]

rules.statement: A job the form marks 'needed for work' goes ahead of other jobs of the same kind.
cites: [A:A01 "Q05 a job the form marks 'needed for work' goes ahead of other jobs of the same kind (major)."]

rules.statement: A bike waiting for a part is listed as 'waiting for parts' and gets no promised date.
cites: [A:A01 "Q06 a bike waiting for a part is listed as 'waiting for parts' and gets no promised date (major)."]

rules.statement: A job over 90 bench minutes is split over two days, never squeezed into one.
cites: [A:A01 "Q07 a job over 90 bench minutes is split over two days, never squeezed into one (major)."]

rules.statement: Ticket numbers are copied exactly as the form gives them.
cites: [A:A01 "Q08 ticket numbers are copied exactly as the form gives them (minor)."]

bad.why: A 'needed for work' job is behind another of the same kind.

risk.notes: A queue can be reordered before the work starts, but a missed promise has already let a customer down. Customers are affected. The worst case is a customer who needs the bike for work being promised a day that can't be kept. Nothing is written to any system, so the queue can be redone before the volunteers start.
cites: [A:A01 "Partly reversible"]
[A:A02 "About sixty customers a month and twelve repair volunteers."]
[A:A01 "A bike promised for a day it can't be ready means a customer without a way to get to work"]
[A:A01 "Reads the typed drop-off forms."]

gates.decision: Approve or reject the repair queue.
cites: [A:A01 "I sign off the queue before it goes on the whiteboard."]
[A:A01 "keep default"]
